newsitem.title: CANADA: Due date extended on certain Repap debt.
newsitem.headline: Due date extended on certain Repap debt.

text.p: Creditors have agreed to extend the July 31 due date on C$270 million of Repap Enterprises Inc's bank debt into the company's third quarter, chairman and chief executive officer George Petty said on Wednesday.
Negotiations with creditors continue regarding US$130 million of convertible debentures due August 1, Petty said in a conference call with reporters.
He said the C$270 million of bank debt will be repaid on the closing of Repap's agreement to sell its Repap USA unit to Consolidated Papers Inc for US$674 million.
The sale of Repap USA is expected to close by the end of Repap's third quarter, he said.
Petty said bids received for the company's coated paper and kraft pulp-making operations in the Canadian province of New Brunswick were not judged acceptable.
"We think there is better value in operating the New Brunswick mill on a stand-alone basis in the improving market environment in which we find ourselves," Petty said.
He said Repap is not soliciting offers for the New Brunswick operations.

Chief financial officer Ronald Sumner said Repap expects that under improving market conditions, the company will be able to recapitalize its New Brunswick unit, which carries about C$1 billion of debt.
"There are a number of successful one-mill companies and we expect this to be one," Sumner said.
Sumner said that New Brunswick's liquidity needs "will be looked after internally," and the company expects to be able to move foward without filing for court protection from creditors.

Repap officials said financial details of the company's agreement to sell its kraft paper and lumber operations in The Pas, Manitoba to closely-held Tolko Industres Ltd will be available within seven to 10 days.
Sumner declined to divulge the value of the Manitoba transaction, but said he expects the sale price to exceed the unit's roughly C$95 million of debt.

Turning to industry conditions, Petty said prices for benchmark no. 5, 40-lb. coated paper had improved by about US$140 a ton from their first-quarter 1997 trough to reach US$860 a ton. Coated paper prices remain about US$400 a ton below their fourth-quarter 1995 peak, he said.
Prices for kraft pulp have improved by US$50 a metric ton from their first-quarter trough to reach US$610 a tonne, Petty said.

Stephen Larson, president and chief operating officer, said that Repap plans to retain some of its Repap USA sales staff to sell and distribute its coated paper in the United States. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
